assessment.calibration_basis: Scorecard gives p_engine=0.55 (the 0.55 customer-denial floor plus a +0.5-weighted recent-card-testing/CNP adjustment, since R7's recurring-charge exception did not clear the denial) against a very low raw calibration cal_p=0.0555 and a flagged families_conflict=true. I moved slightly above p_engine to 0.60, within the +/-0.10 band, weighting the memory family more heavily: prior_cases_for_customer shows 10 prior confirmed-fraud closed cases on this exact card (CC-4501, CC-3905, CC-3206, CC-3039, CC-2799, CC-2673, CC-2247, CC-1056, CC-0290, CC-0031), six of them the same card_not_present_new_device template, plus a live card_testing shape found on the card only 20 days earlier (card_testing_check). I did not push toward the fraud band (>=0.70) because the flagged transaction's own cms_p is only 0.043, the scorecard marks the scorer unreliable at this card's transaction volume (card_seq 10307 of 10312), no strong device/ring corroborates this specific transaction (shared_origin_scan: is_strong=false for every device on this card, including the flagged one), and episode_candidates found no sig_match tying 3583368 to neighboring chain members, so the graph picture genuinely conflicts with the denial-driven floor and the prior-case memory.
